reasoning_content: Interesting: `ls /workspace/app/node_modules` returned 0 entries, and `.bin` had no nx. Wait, earlier `ls /workspace/app/node_modules/.pnpm | wc -l` returned 1782. So `.pnpm` has 1782 entries, yet the top level of node_modules is 0? Let me check more carefully — the top-level node_modules might be empty, or it might be a pnpm virtual store only. Let's take a look.

action.command: ls -la /workspace/app/node_modules/ | head -20; echo "==="; ls /workspace/app/node_modules/.pnpm | head -5; echo "==="; ls /workspace/app/node_modules/.pnpm | grep -i "nx\|angular" | head -5; echo "==="; ls -la /workspace/cms/node_modules/ | head -10

tool_call.name: terminal
tool_call.arguments: {"command": "ls -la /workspace/app/node_modules/ | head -20; echo \"===\"; ls /workspace/app/node_modules/.pnpm | head -5; echo \"===\"; ls /workspace/app/node_modules/.pnpm | grep -i \"nx\\|angular\" | head -5; echo \"===\"; ls -la /workspace/cms/node_modules/ | head -10", "summary": "Inspect node_modules top-level contents", "security_risk": "LOW"}
